To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the effectiveness of learning activities depends on the degree of cognitive load imposed by the learning task, which in turn depends on task complexity and the amount of supportive information, and (2) the effectiveness of cognitive load depends on the degree to which learning tasks are authentic, on task complexity, on the expertise of the coordinator, and on the amount of supportive in-formation.
the learning of software maintenance tasks in offshoring projects is most effective when tasks are authentic, moderately complex, and well specified, and when supportive information is available.

learning effectiveness is influenced by the expertise and experience of the onsite coordinator; by the complexity of the learning task; by the degree of specification of the learning task and the availability of supportive information; and by cultural and semantic distances between the onsite and offshore locations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the transition phase in offshoring projects can be effectively managed.
the cognitive load imposed on the onsite team by learning tasks during software maintenance offshoring projects.
the effectiveness of learning activities in the transition phase of offshoring projects and contributes to the literature by providing empirical insights into the cognitive load of learning tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of learning tasks with moderate cognitive load and supportive information is most effective.
the learning effectiveness of learning tasks is influenced by the expertise, the complexity of the task, the specification of the task, and the supportive information.
the effectiveness of learning activities in offshoring projects is influenced by the complexity of the learning task, the degree of task specification, and the availability of supportive information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
learning activities should be carefully selected and sequenced in order to avoid excessive cognitive load.
the transition phase is not a time for learning, but for doing, and that learning is a consequence of doing.
learning activities in the transition phase of offshoring projects should be designed with the aim to minimize cognitive load and to support the transfer of knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learning tasks that are authentic, specific, and impose moderate cognitive load are most effective in the context of software maintenance offshoring.
learning tasks should be designed to be authentic and to impose moderate cognitive load.
learning tasks should be carefully selected and designed to ensure learning effectiveness.
